title: Ambulatory estimates of maximal aerobic power from foot-ground contact times and heart rates in running humans
claims: Accelerometer-derived foot-ground contact times were highly correlated with contact times measured by a treadmill-mounted force plate.
On average, accelerometric contact times were 14.6 ± 0.5% longer than those measured from the force plate.
The longer accelerometer-derived contact times arose mainly from the later portion of the contact period, when no force is exerted.
